summary: A step's capacity raises its seat's lane while the seat holds the step, and a step whose raised lane does not fit its host waits blocked with why

replay.detail: No claim or projection changes. A waiting step uses the existing blocked state and reason.

rules.detail: Where lanes are on, a ready step that declares a capacity and is assigned to one of this host's laned seats becomes ready only when the raised lane fits the host's room for lanes (the same accounting as a seat start); until then it is blocked with a reason starting `step lane`, tried again each pass. A step whose capacity would lower the lane of a seat declared outside its publication waits with that reason too. While a laned seat holds such a step (assigned and ready, or claimed), its live slice is raised with systemctl --user set-property --runtime, and set back when it no longer does: cores at once, memory once the lane holds less than the seat's own lane allows. Admission counts the raised lane, and counts a raise it admits at once, so two steps judged in one pass do not take the same room. A daemon that restarts reads each laned seat's slice (cpu.max, memory.max) before it has set one itself, so a raise left from before the restart is lowered the same way and counted until then.

compatibility.detail: Local to each daemon. An older member runs a declared step in its seat's own lane. A step this build blocks with a `step lane` reason is tried again by any build that has #4616 (which ships that retry first), so on such a build it is delivered as before, without a raise. A run owner rolled back below #4616 leaves such a step blocked until it upgrades again.

downtime.detail: Takes effect when the daemon runs this build on a host with lanes on.

recovery.detail: Reverting this change stops raising lanes for steps; a build with #4616 still tries again a step blocked for room, which then becomes ready without a raise. A slice raised at the time keeps its raise until its seat's next launch. Rolling a run owner back below #4616 leaves a step blocked with a `step lane` reason until that host upgrades.
